To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

‘the palm groves of the Canary Islands, Cyprus and Crete are threatened by habitat loss and fragmentation, and the conservation of their wild populations and the associated habitat types should be improved by the European Union.’

the conservation of Phoenix palm grove habitats in the European Union should include all native populations of P. canariesis and P. theopharsti, as well as the wild populations of P. thephrasti and P. dactyifera.
the current definition of Phoenix palm grove in the Habitats directive is inadequate for the conservation of the European populations of P. canaries, P. dacylifera and P. Theophrasti.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conservation of Phoenix palm grove habitats in the European Union.
the protection and conservation of the wild-growing populations and habitats of Phoenix palms in the European Union.

the conservation of the three Phoenix species and the habitats that they create, in the EU, in order to ensure the maintenance of their genetic and species diversity and the ecological services that they provide.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the palm grove habitat type of the Habitats Directive, which currently includes P. canariense and P. theoprasti, should be extended to cover the western group of Phoenix dactyliferas, which is found in the European Union, and all the habitats of P. theophrasti, which is not found there.
the palm groves of all three species of Phoenix in the European Union should be considered for conservation.
the palm groves of P. dacytlifera and P canariensis should be considered as one single habitat type (9370*).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is an urgent need to re-evaluate and redefine the conservation status of Phoenix palm grove habitats in the EU.
the palm groves of the European Union are a mosaic of habitats, which are not only of high ecological value but are also important for cultural and economic reasons.

, in the EU, the conservation of the habitat type ‘Palm grove of Phoenix’ should include all the habitats of the three Phoenix species, and the conservation of the habitats of the species should be included in the EU Habitats Directive, as a priority.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order for the Habitats Directive to be effective, the definition of habitats must be updated to reflect the current situation on the ground.
, in order for palm groves to be effectively protected and managed, they should be recognized and classified as a habitat of European interest.
, in the European context, the conservation of Phoenix palms is not only a Mediterranean issue, but a European one, with implications for conservation management and policy at the European scale.
